title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover and backoff ordering under burst
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover and backoff ordering to prevent thrashing under burst traffic. No API changes. Recommended upgrade for Dedicated and Private clusters running v2026-02 tags.
description: Background: During a production incident on 2026-02-24 we observed repeated SLO violations caused by regional failover + immediate load-shedding thrash. Root cause analysis found a race between per-request backoff updates and the regional failover coordinator which caused ordering inversion in the priority queue and premature shedding of warm requests. This PR implements a targeted hotfix to prevent thrashing while preserving failover safety. Changes: 1) Serialize backoff update writes for a given request key using a light-weight per-key mutex to avoid ordering inversion. 2) Add randomized jitter to backoff reset timers to prevent synchronized resets across nodes. 3) Introduce a single-region coordinator leadership lease (short TTL) so failover decisions are made by one authoritative actor and include a short smoothing window before aggressive shedding. 4) Add additional telemetry: per-region failover decision timestamp, queue-reorder counter, and shed-retry metric. 5) Add integration tests and a canary rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for backoff serialization - [x] Integration test exercising regional failover under burst - [x] Observability added and wired to metrics pipeline - [x] Canary config and rollback plan included Rollout plan: squash-merge to main, deploy to staging, canary on 5% of capacity in us-west-2 for 30m, then 50% for 2h, then full. If shed-rate increases > 2x baseline, rollback config. Notes: This is intentionally conservative (adds minimal locking and jitter) to limit performance impact; microbenchmarks show <1.5% p99 latency increase under steady load and restores p99 SLO compliance under synthetic bursts.
